value.text: {"result": {"suggestions": [{"kind": "new_thesis", "ticker": "GOOGL", "statement": "TPUs become a merchant-style product that Google deploys in third-party facilities for external customers, creating a Cloud revenue line distinct from its internal capacity needs.", "wrong_if": "Reported TPU deployments in third-party facilities are cancelled, are not contracted for external customers, or prove to serve only Google's internal capacity.", "driver_ids": ["GOOGL.cloud_growth", "GOOGL.capex"], "rationale": "First-hand channel checks describe Google-managed TPU pods in colo and neocloud sites serving external customers, a merchant-hardware debate that the existing pillars on Search clicks, capex-driven margin pressure and regulatory remedies do not address.", "claim_ids": ["synthetic_000049.c1", "synthetic_000049.c3", "synthetic_000049.c4"], "sections": [{"email_id": "synthetic_000049", "quote": "Two of the three colo operators and one neocloud contact independently described Google-managed TPU pods being installed, or contracted for installation, in third-party facilities."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000049", "quote": "One operator said the contract has a take-or-pay structure with a 5-year term."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000049", "quote": "The former Google contact said the purpose is to serve external customers who want TPU capacity inside their own preferred regions or near existing GPU clusters, rather than to relieve Google's internal capacity."}]}], "no_change_reason": null}}
